narrationTexts: Let me see the established pattern from an already-migrated file, and the db.execute definition.
Vendor is marked do-not-edit, so I'll leave it and flag it. Migrating the 12 first-party files:
finalText:
Migration finished. 36 call sites across 12 files, matching the `db.execute({ sql, params })` shape already used by the migrated files:

- `accounts`: `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`
- `support`: `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js`
- `orders`: `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js`
- `billing`: `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js`
- `catalog`: `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js`
- `analytics`: `repo/cohort.js`

All files pass `node --check`.

Two things I deliberately did not touch:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** still has 2 `db.query` calls. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost — so patching it in place would be undone. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix: upgrade the vendored package, or wrap the adapter so it calls `execute`. Your call — say the word and I'll do either.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls (one per repo file) — different object, unrelated API, left as is.
